B01AF03 is the Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical (ATC) classification code for edoxaban, a direct oral anticoagulant ([[doac|DOAC]]) [^src3]. In the Danish healthcare system, this drug code is centrally tracked within the national clinical quality indicators for patients diagnosed with atrial fibrillation ([[atrieflimren]]) [^src1]. Specifically, B01AF03 is utilized to measure the quality of anticoagulation treatment ([[antikoagulationsbehandling]]) and to monitor kidney function in this patient population [^src1].

Within the registries managed by the Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram (RKKP), B01AF03 is grouped alongside other oral anticoagulants to define treatment cohorts. These include vitamin K antagonists ([[b01aa|B01AA]]) and other DOACs such as dabigatran ([[b01ae07|B01AE07]]), rivaroxaban ([[b01af01|B01AF01]]), and apixaban ([[b01af02|B01AF02]]) [^src1] [^src4] [^src5]. The code serves as a critical data point for calculating denominators and numerators in quality indicators, such as the time to initiation of anticoagulation therapy and the performance of follow-up diagnostics like echocardiography and TSH measurements [^src2] [^src5]. By standardizing the coding of edoxaban and similar medications, the Danish Atrial Fibrillation Database ensures consistent, evidence-based tracking of cardiovascular care across all regions [^src3].
